title: Unità 4 · A tavola!
question: What do I like to eat, and how do I order?
workingOn: food words, the, mi piace, and ordering politely
canDo: I can order food and beverages in a café or restaurant.
I can talk about a variety of foods using definite articles.
I can express food preferences using piacere.
culture: Italian breakfast (la colazione) is light: often a cappuccino and a cornetto, drunk standing up at the bar, which in Italy is a café, not a pub. Lunch and dinner are bigger meals, and dinner is often at 8 pm or later. In restaurants the bill may include a coperto (a small cover charge per person), and big tips are not expected the way they are in the US.

grammar.head: the: il, lo, la, l' (one) · i, gli, le (more). Mi piace + one thing, mi piacciono + more things.
tricks: Masculine: il for most words, lo before s + consonant, z, or y (lo zucchero, lo yogurt), l' before a vowel. Feminine: la, or l' before a vowel.
Plural: il → i; lo and masculine l' → gli; la and feminine l' → le.
Mi piace la pizza (one thing). Mi piacciono gli spaghetti (more than one). Ti piace? = Do you like?
Vorrei = I would like. Learn it as a memorized phrase for ordering politely; you will see how it works in Italiano 3.

sentences: I'd like a sandwich and a water.
The ice cream is super good!

trick: la pizza, la pasta, la cena.

forms.why: Masculine, starts with a normal consonant: il.
trick: il panino, il gelato, il conto.

forms.why: Masculine word starting with z: lo.
trick: lo zucchero, lo yogurt, lo zaino.
Drop the a and add an apostrophe: l'insalata.

forms.why: la pasta is one thing → piace.
i biscotti is more than one → piacciono.
il gelato is one thing → piace.
trick: look at the food, not the person

forms.why: le patatine is more than one → piacciono.
trick: look at the food, not the person

fill.why: la pizza is one thing → piace.
Masculine word with y → lo yogurt.
Vorrei = I would like: the polite way to order.
Il conto, per favore = The check, please.

read.title: Al bar
passage: Sono le otto. Giulia è al bar con Marco.
It's eight o'clock. Giulia is at the café with Marco.
Giulia: «Vorrei un cappuccino e un cornetto, per favore.»
Giulia: "I'd like a cappuccino and a croissant, please."
Marco ha sete: prende un succo d'arancia.
Marco is thirsty: he gets an orange juice.

questions.why: Vorrei un cappuccino e un cornetto, per favore.

questions.q: Marco ha fame o ha sete?

frames: No, non mi piace la pizza.
No, non mi piacciono gli spaghetti.

listen.q: Sei al bar. Un caffè o un cappuccino?
listen.en: You're at the café. A coffee or a cappuccino?

lines: Sì! Mi piace la pizza margherita.
Va bene. E dopo il gelato? 🍦
Certo! Il gelato mi piace tanto!
Of course! I really like ice cream!

prompts: Sì, mi piace … / No, non mi piace …
Sì, mi piacciono … / No, non mi piacciono …

finish: Now I know how to say what food I like and how to order at an Italian café!

idiom.ex: È l'una e ho una fame da lupo!
idiom.exEn: It's one o'clock and I'm starving!
idiom.note: Literally 'to have a wolf's hunger.' Said when you are very, very hungry. It uses avere, like ho fame.

flags: Vorrei is condizionale (Italiano 3). It is taught ONLY as a memorized phrase, as you approved; trick 4 tells students so.
Reading uses 'al bar' (articulated preposition), 'ha sete' and 'prende' (regular -ere verb); all three are glossed as chunks.
Parla prompt 3 has the waiter say 'Che cosa desidera?' (formal 'What would you like?'). It is not in the vocab; introduce it orally in class or swap it.
Indefinite articles un / una / un' (Vorrei un caffè, un'acqua) are assumed known from Unit 1. Confirm.
Chat chunks not taught in a chart: Anch'io, Va bene, dopo, Certo, tanto (all glossed); 'pizza margherita' is a name.
Spelling: il menù (with accent) chosen; il menu (no accent) is also correct and common. Pick one for the whole game.
il caffè is glossed as espresso coffee: in Italy un caffè means an espresso. Worth saying in class.
Culture facts are unverified: coperto is common but not universal, tipping norms and dinner times vary by region.
Trap 'Ha freddo' in the reading uses avere + freddo, assumed known from the Il tempo unit.
